A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same token-cleaning work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, proofs, tables, figures, and examples, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments across three base models and seven benchmarks, with sensitivity studies, checkpoint results, and token-selection examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds fixed-model and RHO sensitivity results and token-score diagnostics.

M1.justification: Equations 2–4, global token ranking, both cleaning strategies, and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedures. Appendix B explains existing loss masking without introducing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five-source, 50k-sample SFT pool and seven evaluation benchmarks. The added analyses use retained models, data, and tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds RHO to the token-proportion comparison in Table 7, which previously reported only self-evolving cleaning. RHO already appeared in the main comparison; the main baseline set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 extends the token-proportion sweep to fixed-model cleaning and RHO, reporting settings beyond their previous default of 0.6. Existing data partitions, evaluation metrics, model sizes, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The proportion sensitivity analysis now covers fixed-model cleaning and RHO alongside self-evolving cleaning. New Appendix E.4 and Figure 3 examine token-loss separation across four iterations and three base models. Existing checkpoint and reference-model analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 3 displays token losses, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds fixed-model and RHO results at nondefault proportions; for example, their reported averages at 0.5 are 51.90 and 52.10 on LLaMA-3.2-3B. Figure 3 adds score-distribution findings. Tables 1–6 and 8 and the retained self-evolving rows of Table 7 preserve their numerical results.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, error bound, corollary, and full appendix proof are unchanged mathematically. Corollary 5.1.1 becomes Corollary 5.2, and the proof moves from Appendix Section 9 to Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: noisy-label token cleaning, fixed and self-evolving strategies, theoretical error bounds, and downstream performance benefits. The headline improvement claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly clarifies that loss masking provides no training speedup or GPU-memory reduction and argues that inference costs match RHO. Appendix E.4 interprets increasing token-loss contrast as enabling better selection. Existing model-scale and data-scale limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and explains loss masking and inference workload in Appendix B. The disclosed LoRA settings, batch size, learning rate, input length, hardware, and approximate training time are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hu et al. (2022) for LoRA and removes the Liu et al. (2020) LogiQA citation and reference while retaining that benchmark. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to prior token selection remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained, with limited terminology edits, new acknowledgment and impact statements, and reorganized appendix headings. The illustrative examples are reordered, and the application-metric response is shortened.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper throughout the main text and references, substantially changing display sizes and placement. Figure 2 gains a fixed-model curve, Figure 3 adds twelve diagnostic panels, and Tables 6–7 introduce explicit token-proportion columns, with Table 7 expanded into three method blocks.

improvement.justification: v2 provides better sensitivity evidence through the expanded Table 7 and supporting diagnostics in Figure 3. Appendix B resolves ambiguity about computational savings, and the new code link improves reproducibility information. These are useful, limited gains in support and transparency; the central method, proofs, and headline results remain unchanged.
